A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same auxiliary-classifier continual-learning study. All 25 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures that support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original CIFAR100 and ImageNet100 experiments measuring classification accuracy, representation stability and inference cost, with further experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on VGG19, longer task sequences, overthinking and individual auxiliary classifiers.

M1.justification: Both versions use jointly trained auxiliary classifiers, weighted classifier losses, maximum-confidence static prediction and threshold-based early exit with the same fallback rule in Equation 1. VGG19 and DER++ apply the existing approach without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR100 and ImageNet100 for image classification, including class-incremental and warm-start experiments. The additional CIFAR100 task partitions, network configurations and joint-training control change experimental design within this coverage.

E2.justification: DER++ is newly evaluated in the main and warm-start comparisons. The ViT comparison expands from five methods in v2 Figure 22 to eleven in v3 Figure 16, adding ANCL, ER, GDumb, EWC, FT and DER++ within that experiment.

E3.justification: v3 adds VGG19 configurations with 6, 10 and 18 ACs, CIFAR100 partitions into 20 and 50 tasks, and growing exemplar memory for the 50-task experiment. It also introduces an i.i.d. joint-training control, normalized overthinking diagnostics and single-AC experiments with classifier loss weight 1. The original main benchmark protocols remain.

E4.justification: New analyses compare overthinking against joint training (Section 3.3), isolate individual ACs (Appendix C.4), and examine classifier selection and accuracy during inference (Appendix E.2). VGG19 experiments further test classifier density. Existing diversity, oracle-bound, gradient-propagation and inference-rule analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v3 removes variability bands from many corresponding classifier-accuracy and dynamic-inference plots, including v2 Figures 2 and 17-21 versus v3 Figures 3 and 10-12, while retaining tabular ± reporting. It also qualifies v2's general three-seed statement with a single-seed ViT exception. These substantially change uncertainty disclosure without establishing that retained experiments used fewer runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 preserves the original methods' scores but adds DER++ and recalculates averages. v3 adds substantial VGG19, longer-sequence and diagnostic results. Existing entries also change: six-task warm-start BiC baseline/+AC accuracy changes from 45.87/48.99 in v2 Table 2 to 46.60/48.75 in v3 Table 3.

T1.justification: The formal prediction rules, Equation 1 and oracle construction are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is introduced; the added analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The central claims of reduced forgetting, approximately 10% relative accuracy improvement and computational savings remain. v3 adds a headline claim that continual learning exhibits more overthinking than i.i.d. training and emphasizes larger-network scalability. The conclusion revises maximum stated inference savings from 70% to 60%.

C2.justification: v3 develops explanations involving elevated overthinking, distillation restricting classifier diversity, VGG's absence of residual connections and ViT miscalibration. Its single-AC analysis identifies opportunities to optimize placement. The limitations now explicitly identify the vision/classification boundary while dropping v2's more detailed discussion of additional hyperparameters and simple dynamic-inference design.

D1.justification: v3 documents VGG classifier placement and loss-weight increments, explicitly identifies ViT-b-16, and specifies the 1%-100% confidence-threshold grid. Most ResNet/ViT training recipes and exemplar-processing details are retained as Appendix K becomes Appendix A. The anonymized code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of Liu et al. (2020b) and Yan et al. (2024), replacing v2's blanket claim of no prior intermediate-classifier work in continual learning with a distinction based on its general offline framework. It also adds transfer-learning, VGG and ViT references while removing several early-exit citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, analysis and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around overthinking and efficiency. Warm-start experiments and ResNet ablations move into reorganized appendices, implementation details move to the first appendix, and title, author information and impact-statement text change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout. Dynamic-inference curves are extensively regrouped, per-classifier accuracy plots become positive-only differences, and a network diagram plus new experimental displays are added. Numerous retained figures and tables move between the main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: The joint-training comparison, individual-AC controls, VGG19 experiments and expanded ViT comparisons strengthen questions about mechanism and generality that v2 tested less directly. The related-work discussion also qualifies the earlier blanket novelty claim. These gains are partly offset by lost variability bands, positive-only accuracy displays and overbroad statements: Appendix B.2 claims improvement throughout, although Table 4 reports ANCL decreasing from 5.88 to 5.54 on 50 tasks. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
